original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Price the flag-9 entry of the I - G/2 side correction (Y23 += -G[23,4]/2 X4 = +1/2 X4) at the published end-cut (terminal Y23 transport 3489), with no co-hosted repair. Build and natively validate four corrected words on the published word (target lift T, source detour S, one private-copy lifetime P, and the whole Y23 row T48), give their exact before/after bills, and prove the matching obstruction: in the class that keeps the published events and ADDs, keeps endpoint frames, may retarget or insert transports, and keeps the private register C's published lifetimes, no placement of the correction ADD at any of the 25 insertion classes costs zero added rank mass, so the strict minimum is exactly 2. Recompute and cite open #3614's primary feeder X58:333 at leave 745; do not reopen the deferred flag-9 head-step repair.
scope_change_reason: Open #3614's forcing census finds flag 9's primary entry (23,4) needs non-private +2 on the published word (feeder X58:333 at leave 745; 25/25 insertion classes zero-mass obstructed) but constructs no attaining correction. Open #3601/#3610 price flags 43 and 1 at co-hosted repairs; flag 9's head-step repair is deferred. This package answers #3614 OQ2 for flag 9 by building attaining end-cut words on the published chronology (#3443) and confirming the private-copy discount route.
bottleneck_link: On the published word the end-cut correction for flag 9's entry needs a common chart for X4 and Y23. From event 745 on, X4's forced frame contains X58's head 333, while Y23 stays inside its final hyperplane, which excludes 333. The cheapest strict correction therefore pays +2 rank mass, attained by T, S and T48. Only the inherited private-copy contract lowers it to +1. Neither is a supplier. No co-hosted discount is claimed (deferred repair not reopened).
stop_rule: Stop after flag 9: one entry, one target row, one published end-cut (3489), four validated words and the zero-mass obstruction over all insertion classes. Do not touch flags 0, 1 or 43, the other 103 target rows, global hosting, precision or kappa. Do not reopen deferred flag-9 head-step repair or leave-alone #3601/#3610/#3614/#3532/#3508.
evidence: Flag-9 entry: G[23,4]=-1, so I-G/2 needs +1/2 X4 in Y23. On the published word the corrections replace the terminal Y23 transport at 3489 (A3=[447,127,192] -> F23, rank 5). T: Y23 A3->FULL (rank 6), ADD in FULL, FULL->F23 (rank 1): +2 events, +1 ADD, +1 transport occurrence, +2 rank mass, profile H1-H5+H6 vs published, 741 edges. S: published transport, then X4 FULL->F23, ADD in F23, F23->FULL: +3 events, +1 ADD, +2 transport occurrences, +2 rank mass, profile 2H1, 742 edges. P: zero C at FULL, copy X4, C FULL->F23, ADD, erase: +5 events, +1 ADD, +1 transport occurrence, +1 rank mass, profile H1, private lifetimes 8->9, 741 edges. T48: the T lift carrying all 48 off-diagonal entries of row 23: +49 events, +48 ADDs, +1 transport occurrence, +2 rank mass; Y23's final row is exactly y23 + x23. The unchanged check_native.validate() passes each coefficient-0 word (native edges incl. three newly lowered A3->FULL and FULL<->F23 recipes, 208 adapters, 280 framed rows, 72 dirty helpers) and rejects each real word only at 'full physical boundary endpoint Y23'; exact rational replay changes only Y23's row. Obstruction: at event 745 (G7 -= 2 X4) X4's frame leaves F23 carrying X58's head 333 along carrier path 631:G7<-X58, 729:G16<-X58, 731:G16<-X35, 745:G7<-X4; G[23,58]=0 puts 333 outside Y23's final; a least-lower-bound sweep blocks all 25 insertion classes; 7/7 early private deliveries before C's published span are blocked. Per-register added rank mass is even, so the strict minimum is exactly 2. Feeder/obstruction consistent with open #3614 (leave-alone). Selected kappa unchanged.

open_questions.question: Is the +1 private-copy route P admissible as a physical correction, or must every side-correction lifetime be reversibly uncomputed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: P is cheaper than every strict route only because the inherited private-copy contract lets C be discarded while it holds a copy of X4. If that contract is not admissible for corrections, the strict bound of +2 per corrected target applies.
open_questions.first_step: Price an uncompute of C (copy back to zero in X4's chart before the erase) and compare its rank cost with S.
open_questions.blocked_by: The native channel package labels the private-copy semantics as inherited and makes no reversibility claim.

open_questions.question: If a co-hosted flag-9 repair later lands (after #3532 merges and shared headstep.py), does the end-cut +2 discount at that cut?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Flag 1's R1 chart made the entry free (+0 vs R1). Flag 9's deferred repair is not reopened here; an analogous R1-style free-ride would be the first co-host discount for this flag.
open_questions.first_step: After a published co-hosted flag-9 chart exists, re-run the T/E comparison of #3610 at that chart.
open_questions.blocked_by: research/p104-flag9-head-step-repair remains deferred for soft-overlap with open #3532.
